newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: FORECAST - Swiss growth consensus drops for 1997.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Swiss growth consensus drops for 1997.

text.p: A quarterly consensus of Swiss economic forecasts published on Tuesday dropped its target for 1997 growth to 0.6 percent, reflecting a round of downward revisions since its last forecast of 1.14 percent in September,

The Business Economists' Consensus, a survey of 33 public and private sector economists, found stronger recovery from six years of stagnation was not expected until 1998, when gross domestic product (GDP) is projected to rise by 1.66 percent.
The forecasts were derived from a poll by the Swiss Association of Business Economists.

Swiss growth has been near zero on average since 1990. Hopes for recovery have dwindled as GDP forecasts for 1997 have been cut back in recent months to between zero and one percent. The economy is widely estimated to have contracted by 0.75 percent this year.

The report said the drop in its 1997 consensus forecast to 0.6 percent from September's 1.14 percent estimate resulted from "lower than expected growth in construction and fixed asset investments as well as in exports."
Its 1998 forecast of 1.66 percent was a first-time estimate with no comparable figure from the September survey.
